CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation for breast reduction.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female presenting for consultation regarding breast reduction. The patient has been considering this procedure for approximately 6-7 years. She reports a long-standing history of back pain, neck pain, and upper back pain since high school, which she attributes in part to her breast size. She has been attending chiropractor visits for a few years. The patient experiences bra strap indentations on her shoulders and reports occasional numbness and tingling in her hands. She notes that her breasts are always sweaty but denies rashes underneath. The patient reports that her activities are limited due to breast size, particularly with working out, jumping, or running, which causes pain. She currently wears a 34E sports bra as it is more comfortable than regular bras in her size. The patient has not had previous consultation for breast reduction. She has not had any mammograms but is aware of family history of breast cancer and knows she should start screening at age 30. She has lost approximately 10 pounds over the past few months and desires to lose an additional 20 pounds. She would ideally like to achieve a B cup size post-operatively.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for back pain, neck pain, upper back pain, occasional numbness and tingling in hands, and excessive sweating underneath breasts. Denies rashes underneath breasts, nipple discharge, or breast masses.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Propranolol (migraine medication).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Positive for breast cancer in mother, who was diagnosed at age 40.

SOCIAL HISTORY
The patient is currently studying psychology. She drinks wine on occasion. She denies tobacco and drug use. She has no children currently but may plan to have children in the future. She is married; her husband recently accepted a new job and will be switching insurance plans in July.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Inspection reveals asymmetrical breasts with severe ptosis bilaterally. No nipple retraction or discharge bilaterally. No breast tenderness, masses, or axillary lymphadenopathy is palpable. One breast is noted to be slightly lower than the other. Current bra size approximately G cup; patient reports wearing 34E sports bra.

RESULTS
Measurements obtained. Body surface area 2.65. Minimum required resection based on Schnur scale is 1,792 grams. Given extremely large breasts, there is potential for using a nipple graft.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Julia Jones is a 25-year-old female with symptomatic macromastia presenting for evaluation of breast reduction. The patient is an ideal candidate for bilateral reduction mammoplasty. Patient has attempted nonsurgical treatments with minimal relief. Surgical plan discussed: bilateral reduction mammoplasty with anchor incision technique, removal of breast tissue and fat, nipple elevation, anticipated final size small C cup (patient desired B cup). Surgery anticipated to take approximately 3 hours with placement of drains bilaterally to remain for approximately 1 week. Patient to remain overnight in hospital for pain control and monitoring. Discussed risks and benefits including: potential for altered or absent nipple sensation (though generally nipple sensation preserved unless massive reduction), post-operative bruising, breastfeeding success uncertain (approximately 30% of patients unable to breastfeed post-reduction), and breast changes with future pregnancy and weight gain/loss. Activity restrictions for 6 weeks post-operatively including no heavy lifting and no driving for 2-3 weeks. Scar management with clear plastic tape; scars typically red initially and take approximately 1 year to mature. Patient anticipates proceeding with surgery once insurance changes in July. Plan to obtain photos today for insurance submission. Office to submit for insurance approval once patient provides new insurance information. Pre-operative meeting to be scheduled once surgery approved to review final instructions and answer additional questions.
